title: Dr. Murphy Asked for a Floor. Dr. Oz Sent a “Certificado de Excelencia”
description: On August 3, 2026, Rep. Dr. Greg Murphy and 13 House Republicans asked HHS Secretary Kennedy for one thing: a Medicare Advantage benchmark floor for Puerto Rico at 70% of the national average for 2028, the level the U.S. Virgin Islands already gets under the "similar area" clause of Section 1876. On September 14, CMS answered over Dr. Mehmet Oz's signature: the views will be taken into account for 2028, the current approach is consistent with its statutory authorities, and look at what was already done for 2027, a 4.4% adjustment for the propensity of zero claims and a D-SNP exception. This episode reads both letters and a 12-year administrative record. Puerto Rico's benchmarks sit about 41% below the national average and the gap has widened since 2012. Some 670,000 seniors, 96% of those eligible, are in Medicare Advantage, yet the rates are set from the bills of the 29,000 in traditional Medicare, on an island with no Medicare Savings Program, no SSI and no standard SNAP. CMS's reasons for refusing a floor have changed five times since 2016 while it found the discretion for other fixes. And the San Juan wage index, down 14.26% from FY2024 to FY2027 on a locked 5%-a-year step-down, is about to be repriced into the 2028 rates. Congratulations on the performance. Here is less money.
